mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה holds that only a man-made אהל counts as an אהל for טומאת מת. The גמרא gives his source and then challenges it from the oxen used in the פרה אדומה procedure.
overview: רבי יהודה learns from a גזירה שוה with the משכן that only a man-made אהל counts for טומאת מת. The רבנן instead read the repeated word אהל as a ריבוי that includes any covering. The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה from a משנה in מסכת פרה. In that משנה, pure children rode on doors placed on oxen to fetch water from the שילוח, and a ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying they used only oxen, with no doors. That seems to show him relying on the ox's body, which no person made, as an אהל. רב דימי answers in the name of רבי אלעזר: רבי יהודה agrees that a natural covering counts once it is a fistbreadth, and a ברייתא about caves and rock cavities supports this. The גמרא then asks why doors, which are several fists wide, were excluded. אביי answers that doors were simply unnecessary. רבא answers that doors were avoided because a child on a wide door might stick out a limb and become טמא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source: the אהל of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from a גזירה שוה between the אהל of a dead person and the אהל of the משכן that only a man-made tent counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'אהל' 'אהל' from the משכן. It is written here: 'This is the law when a man dies in a tent.' And it is written there: 'And he spread the tent over the Tabernacle.' Just as there it was made by a person, so too here it must be made by a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רבי יהודה says that an אהל not made by a person is not an אהל. He learns it by linking the word אהל in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אהל appears in the laws of טומאת מת and also in the building of the משכן. The tent over the משכן was clearly put up by people. So the גזירה שוה teaches that the אהל in the laws of טומאה must also be man-made.

keyTerms.meaning: Tent; any covering that spreads or blocks impurity
It is written here ... and it is written there (the formula of a גזירה שוה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This source is the whole basis of רבי יהודה's rule. The challenge that follows asks whether he truly holds this rule consistently.

phrases.english: He derives 'tent' 'tent' from the Tabernacle.
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה built on the shared word אהל.

phrases.english: It is written here:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the laws of טומאת מת.

phrases.english: 'This is the law when a man dies in a tent' (Numbers 19:14),
and it is written there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the building of the משכן.

phrases.english: 'And he spread the tent over the Tabernacle' (Exodus 40:19),
just as there it was by human hands,
so too here it must be by human hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud about what רבי יהודה's reason is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the man-made tent over the משכן.

steps.title: The רבנן's reading: the repeated word includes more
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the word אהל is repeated many times in the פרשה, and this widens the law to include any covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: 'אהל,' 'אהל' — the תורה included more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה. They read the repeated word אהל as a ריבוי, meaning it adds more cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the word אהל appears again and again in the פרשה of טומאת מת. They treat this repetition as including anything that provides cover, even if no person made it. This blocks the narrowing that רבי יהודה learned from the משכן.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: 'tent,' 'tent' — it included more.
phrases.notes: The repetition widens the law to include even natural coverings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated אהל is a ריבוי that includes non-man-made coverings.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really hold this? A contradiction is raised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really holds that a natural אהל is not an אהל, and announces a contradicting source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יהודה hold that any tent not made by a person is not a tent? They raised a contradiction:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It questions רבי יהודה's rule and tells us a contradicting source is about to be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ורמינהו means 'they set two sources against each other.' Nothing has been proven yet. Steps 4–6 bring the source, and the actual contradiction is stated in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (set sources against each other)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֹהֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי בִּידֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: that any tent that is not made by human hands
is not a tent?
And they raised a contradiction:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining רבי יהודה's rule to challenging it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that a non-man-made אהל is not an אהל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source will show רבי יהודה treating a natural covering as an אהל.

steps.title: Pure courtyards in Jerusalem for raising children
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in מסכת פרה describes courtyards built over hollow space, where children were born and raised in purity for the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were courtyards built in ירושלים on top of the rock, with a hollow space beneath them, because of a possible grave in the depths. They would bring pregnant women, who gave birth there and raised their children there for the פרה אדומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the contradicting source, a משנה about how they kept children totally pure for the פרה אדומה. This is background for the coming question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There might be an unknown grave deep underground (קבר התהום). The hollow space under the courtyards acts as a barrier so that טומאה cannot rise up. Children raised there stay pure, so they can help with the פרה אדומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A grave in the depths, unknown to anyone

steps.confusionAlert: Here חלל means an empty space. It is not the same word as a חלל who is a disqualified כהן.

phrases.english: Courtyards were built in Jerusalem
on top of the rock,
and beneath them was a hollow space,
because of a possible grave in the depths.
And they would bring pregnant women
and they would give birth there
and raise their children there for the red heifer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source announced by ורמינהו.
steps.raayaObject: Background for the challenge against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Children ride on doors atop oxen to fetch water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: the children rode on doors placed on oxen, held stone cups, and filled water at the שילוח. רבי יוסי says they lowered the cups from where they sat.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would bring oxen with doors on their backs. The children sat on the doors, holding stone cups. When they reached the שילוח, they went down into the water, filled the cups, came back up and sat down. רבי יוסי says: each child lowered his cup from his place and filled it, because of a possible grave in the depths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה, describing how the pure children traveled to get water for the פרה אדומה. The doors on the oxen are the key detail for the coming challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doors act as a man-made אהל that protects the children from any hidden grave on the way. Stone cups cannot become טמא. רבי יוסי is even stricter: the children never step down, because there might be a grave right at the water's edge.

keyTerms.meaning: Doors (placed on the oxen as a covering)
Stone cups, which cannot become טמא

phrases.english: And they would bring oxen
with doors on their backs,
and the children would sit on top of them,
with stone cups in their hands.
When they reached the Shiloach,
they went down into the water and filled them,
and came up and sat back down on them.
Rabbi Yosei says:
from his place he would lower the cup and fill it,
because of a possible grave in the depths.
phrases.notes: Even stepping down to the water might put him over a hidden grave.

steps.raayaObject: Shows that doors (a man-made covering) were used to protect the children.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only oxen, no doors
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying they did not bring doors at all, only oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי יהודה says, they did not bring doors, only oxen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי יהודה's own view of the procedure. This is the piece that will create the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no doors were used, the only thing between the child and a possible grave is the ox's body. So רבי יהודה must hold that the ox's body is enough of an אהל to block טומאה.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They would not bring doors,
but only oxen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיוּ מְבִיאִין דְּלָתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יהודה's version of the procedure from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Shows רבי יהודה relying on oxen alone as a barrier.

steps.title: Oxen are not man-made, yet רבי יהודה uses them as a tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the contradiction: an ox is an אהל not made by people, yet רבי יהודה relies on it to block טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But oxen are a tent not made by human hands! And yet it teaches that רבי יהודה says they did not bring doors, only oxen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes its full challenge. רבי יהודה's view about the oxen seems to contradict his rule that only a man-made אהל counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 רבי יהודה learned from the משכן that an אהל must be man-made. Yet here he trusts the body of an ox, which no person made, to work as an אהל. The two sources clash, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns from the משכן that only a man-made אהל counts. The ברייתא about the oxen seems to show him using a natural אהל, and the גמרא must explain this.

phrases.english: But surely oxen

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֹהֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי בִּידֵי אָדָם הוּא,
phrases.english: are a tent that is not made by human hands,
and yet it teaches: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They would not bring doors
but only oxen!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שְׁוָורִים, דְּאֹהֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי בִּידֵי אָדָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradiction from the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule from step 1 that only a man-made אהל counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ox's body is a natural covering, yet רבי יהודה relies on it alone to block טומאה, so he seems to accept a non-man-made אהל.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees once the covering is a fistbreadth
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי אלעזר that רבי יהודה agrees a natural אהל blocks טומאה when it measures a full fistbreadth.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: רבי יהודה agrees that a natural covering counts as an אהל when it is the full size of a fist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 7. רבי יהודה's rule that a natural אהל does not count only applies to small ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man-made אהל needs only a טפח (handbreadth). According to רבי יהודה, a natural אהל needs the larger measure of an אגרוף (fistbreadth). An ox's body is much bigger than a fist, so relying on the oxen fits his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The full size of a fist, a measure larger than a טפח

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key rule for the rest of the passage. According to רבי יהודה, a natural אהל works once it is a fistbreadth. That rule is what makes the door question in Step 10 possible.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael),
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא introduces a teaching brought from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Rabbi Yehuda concedes (it is a tent) when it is the full size of a fist.
phrases.notes: Only a natural אהל smaller than a fist does not count, according to רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule by size: רבי יהודה's view applies only to natural coverings smaller than a fistbreadth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה says no natural covering ever counts as an אהל, so relying on the ox would contradict him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A natural covering of a fistbreadth or more does count for רבי יהודה, and the ox is that big.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this from caves and rock cavities
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה agrees caves and deep rock cavities count as an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: רבי יהודה agrees regarding caves and deep cavities in the rocks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב דימי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Caves and rock hollows are natural, not made by people, yet רבי יהודה treats them as an אהל. This shows that he does not reject every natural אהל. The large ones count, which fits the fistbreadth rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)
Deep cavities or clefts in the rocks

phrases.english: It is also taught so (in a baraita):
And Rabbi Yehuda concedes
regarding caves and deep cavities in the rocks.
phrases.notes: These are natural coverings that still count as an אהל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's claim that רבי יהודה accepts a large natural אהל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about caves and rock cavities.

steps.title: A door is bigger than a fist, so why reject doors?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule: a door is several fistbreadths wide, yet רבי יהודה said they did not bring doors, only oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a door is several fists wide, and yet the ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה said: they did not bring doors, only oxen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 8. If a fist-sized covering is enough, a door should surely be enough too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A door easily passes the fistbreadth size. So why would רבי יהודה exclude doors? It seems to suggest that a door is not a valid אהל, which does not fit the size rule we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at (introduces a challenge from a case)

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי דֶּלֶת, דְּיֵשׁ בָּהּ כַּמָּה אֶגְרוֹפִין,
phrases.english: But there is a door, which measures several fistbreadths,
and it is taught, Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מְבִיאִין דְּלָתוֹת אֶלָּא שְׁוָורִים!
phrases.english: They did not bring doors, only oxen!
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from Step 6.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי דֶּלֶת, דְּיֵשׁ בָּהּ כַּמָּה אֶגְרוֹפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fistbreadth answer of Step 8 using the ברייתא of Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, according to רבי יהודה, anything a fistbreadth or larger counts as an אהל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A door is several fists wide, so it should qualify. רבי יהודה's rejection of doors suggests that size is not what decides the matter.

steps.title: אביי: the doors were simply not needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי יהודה did not reject doors as invalid. Doors were just unnecessary because the oxen were wide enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: they did not need to bring doors.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. רבי יהודה meant that doors were unnecessary, not that they would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox's belly is already more than a fistbreadth, so it blocks the טומאה by itself. Adding a door would be extra and pointless. So the door is a valid אהל according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Abaye said,
they did not need to bring doors.
phrases.notes: The door is fine, just unnecessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, לָא הוּצְרְכוּ לְהָבִיא דְּלָתוֹת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: 'they did not bring' means 'they did not need to bring'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה rejected doors because they are not a valid אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doors are valid, but the oxen alone were enough, so doors were unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: doors were avoided so the child would not stick out a limb
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that they deliberately did not bring doors at all. A child on a wide door feels too secure and might stick his head or a limb out past the edge and become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: they did not bring doors at all, because a child would feel overconfident on it, and perhaps he would stick out his head or one of his limbs and become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same challenge. The door is a valid אהל, but it was avoided for a practical safety reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike אביי, רבא says doors were intentionally kept away. The problem is not the door's status as an אהל. A wide surface makes the child relaxed and careless, and he might reach out beyond the covered area, where there is no protection from the טומאה below. On a narrow ox, the child stays carefully tucked in.

keyTerms.meaning: He feels overconfident or too comfortable

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a natural אהל counts if it is a fistbreadth, so the ox works. Doors are also valid. אביי says they were just unneeded, and רבא says they were avoided because a child on a wide door might stick out a limb and become טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the door fails as an אהל. The door blocks טומאה fine. The worry is only about the child's behavior: a limb sticking out past the door's edge is no longer covered.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מְבִיאִין דְּלָתוֹת כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: they would not bring doors at all,
phrases.notes: Here they avoided doors on purpose, not like אביי's 'they just weren't needed'.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי שֶׁדַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל תִּינוֹק גַּסָּה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: because a child feels overconfident upon it,
perhaps he will stick out his head
or one of his limbs, and become impure
phrases.notes: The limb would extend past the covering, over the possible grave-טומאה below.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לֹא הָיוּ מְבִיאִין דְּלָתוֹת כׇּל עִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 10, different from אביי's in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern: doors were excluded for a safety reason, not because of their אהל status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rejecting doors means doors are not a valid אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doors are a valid אהל, but they were avoided because a child might extend a limb beyond them and become טמא.
